subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<key>.enabled:false` become a hard filesystem/exec deny boundary, or should OpenClaw add a separate strict skill-access policy for that security guarantee?
rationale: The requested fix changes a currently prompt-selection-oriented setting into a security boundary across file access, command execution, sandbox materialization, Gateway/UI state, and docs, so automation cannot choose the product/security contract safely.

options.title: Add an explicit strict skill-access policy
options.body: Introduce a maintainer-approved central policy for hard skill isolation while preserving current `enabled:false` semantics unless deliberately migrated.

options.title: Harden `enabled:false` directly
options.body: Redefine disabled skills as inaccessible and ship compatibility docs, UI wording, and tests for read, exec, and sandbox behavior.

options.title: Document current semantics only
options.body: Keep `enabled:false` as prompt/eligibility filtering and direct operators to sandbox, tool deny lists, and filesystem permissions for hard isolation.

recommendation.title: Add an explicit strict skill-access policy
recommendation.body: Introduce a maintainer-approved central policy for hard skill isolation while preserving current `enabled:false` semantics unless deliberately migrated.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent skill lifecycle hardening and adjacent skill/sandbox history make them the best available owner for the security-boundary choice.
